{{Short description|Estonian politician (1933–2006)}}
[[File:Ülo Tootsen.jpg|thumb|right|Ülo Tootsen]]

'''Ülo Tootsen''' (13 June 1933 – 12 March 2006) was an [[Estonia]]n biologist, journalist, publisher, editor, translator, and politician. He was a member of [[IX Riigikogu]], representing the [[Estonian Centre Party]].<ref name="riigikogu.ee">{{cite web |last1=Sillajõe |first1=Siiri |title=Electoral and legislative data from Estonia |url=https://www.riigikogu.ee/msi_arhiiv/tel321.html |website=www.riigikogu.ee |access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Suri ajakirjanik Ülo Tootsen |url=https://www.ohtuleht.ee/193546/suri-ajakirjanik-ulo-tootsen |publisher=[[Õhtuleht]] |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref>

Tootsen was born in Varstu Parish (now, part of [[Rõuge Parish]]). His brother was journalist, writer and politician [[Toivo Tootsen]]. He graduated from [[University of Tartu|Tartu State University]] in 1957 with a degree in zoology. He then worked in the Ministry of Agriculture of the Estonian SSR in from 1957 until 1959 as a chief [[ichthyology|ichthyologist]]. From 1959 until 1961, he was the cultural editor of the daily newspaper ''[[Rahva Hääl]]''.<ref name="Toots">{{cite web|title=Tootsen, Ülo|url=http://entsyklopeedia.ee/artikkel/tootsen_%C3%BClo|website=Eesti entsüklopeedia|date=2020|access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Suri ajakirjanik Ülo Tootsen |url=https://www.ohtuleht.ee/193546/suri-ajakirjanik-ulo-tootsen |publisher=ohtuleht |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref>

From 1961 until 1991, he worked in the news editorial office of [[Eesti Televisioon]] and worked concurrently at Võru Raadio since 1985 and as a broadcaster for [[Eesti Raadio]].<ref name="Toots" /> From 1991 until 1995, he published the newspaper ''Meelejahutaja'', was the editor of the newspaper ''Elu'' from 1995 until 1996, and was an editor and head of the publications department of ''[[Võrumaa Teataja]]'' from 1996 until 1999. Tootsen has published works in the field of fish farming and journalism, and has translated fiction from the Russian language into Estonian, including works by Vladimir Mitypov, [[Ales Adamovich]], Yevgeny Fadeitshev, [[Feodor Gladkov]], and [[Ion Druță]].<ref name="Toots" /><ref name="riigikogu.ee" />
